clue.text: Treat sadness with pills primarily in jars?

definitions.text: Treat sadness with pills primarily in jars?

indicators.note: jars as a verb means jolts or shakes up, so the letters before it are jumbled
primarily asks for the first letter of the word pills

explanation.surface: A question about whether medication kept in jars is the way to deal with low moods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jars' looks like containers but is a verb meaning shakes, the anagram signal; 'primarily' takes only the first letter of 'pills'. The whole clue also describes what the drugs do.
explanation.definitionFit: Drugs prescribed to lift depression are pills taken to treat sadness, so the whole clue describes them.

clue.text: Baptisms of fire, at the start USA's in round

indicators.note: round suggests turning letters about, so the letters before it are rearranged
at the start asks for the opening letter of the word fire

explanation.surface: A wartime picture: the USA receiving its first experience of combat, as if surrounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baptisms of fire' reads as one phrase, but only 'Baptisms' is the definition; 'of' is anagram fodder, 'at the start' takes the first letter of 'fire', and 'round' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An affusion is a baptism performed by pouring water over the head, a churchly term.

clue.text: Touching man below belt

indicators.note: in a down answer, below puts the word for man under the word for belt

parts.note: to tan someone is to beat or thrash them, as is to belt them
a gent is a gentleman, a man

explanation.surface: A boxing image: punching a man below the belt, a foul blow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'belt' is a verb here, to thrash; in a down light 'below' puts the man under it.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a tangent line just meets a curve, so the word as an adjective means in contact.

clue.text: Drive with more speed, no top covering German racing car

parts.note: Dr is the street-address abbreviation for Drive

indicators.note: covering means the letters that come first wrap around the next piece
no top means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: having more speed is being faster

explanation.surface: A motoring instruction to go faster, roof down, over a German car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no top' drops the first letter to leave ASTER; 'covering' wraps the combined letters around G.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragster is a car built for drag racing, sprinting down a short straight strip.

clue.text: Time to look outside cell

indicators.note: outside means the word for looking surrounds the letter for time

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

explanation.surface: A prisoner reckoning it is time to look beyond their cell.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER is old criminal slang for a prison cell (also a safe).
explanation.definitionFit: In underworld slang a peter is a prison cell, the place where a convict is locked up.

clue.text: Masters entry with sheep, most of flock breaking away

parts.note: Ernie Els, the South African golfer, is a regular entrant in the Masters tournament

indicators.note: breaking means one piece bursts into the middle of another

parts.note: a ewe is a female sheep

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a herd is a flock of animals

explanation.surface: A golf tournament entrant arriving with sheep while most of the flock runs off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' leaves HER, which 'breaking' puts inside the sheep. The Masters is a famous American golf tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away means being in another place, not here, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Range Rover, initially following Queen as one shot bears

indicators.note: bears means carries, so the anagram letters hold the next piece
shot means wrecked or broken, so the two letters of the little word swap places
following means the Rover letter comes after the Queen letters

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letter of the word Rover

explanation.surface: Echoes a Range Rover in a royal shooting party, with the Queen bagging bears in one shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range Rover' is split: 'Range' is the definition. 'shot' makes SA, 'bears' wraps it round the rest, and 'following' puts the Rover letter after the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a jagged mountain range, from the Spanish word for a saw.

clue.text: Cornish town: its leader is not available for locals

indicators.note: its leader is says the first letter of the town is swapped for what follows

parts.note: St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall

explanation.surface: A notice that the head of a Cornish town is away, unavailable to residents.
explanation.walkthrough: The S that begins STIVES is replaced by NA. St Ives is a seaside town in Cornwall, England's south-western county.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives are people born in a place, the residents rather than visitors.

clue.text: More angry really about royal

parts.note: so can mean really, as in so good
re means about or concerning
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: Someone even angrier about a member of the royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: Sore in the informal sense means annoyed, so its comparative means angrier.

clue.text: Match frames to hand painting?

indicators.note: frames means the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: to fit is to match or suit
near means close by, to hand

explanation.surface: Picture-framing talk: matching the frame to a hand-painted piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags painting as only one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: Painting is an example of the creative arts made for beauty, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Top one worrying?

definitions.meaning: a top is a garment for the upper body, like a jumper
someone who sweats is someone anxious or fretting

explanation.surface: A question about a person at the top who frets.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a knitted jumper and, literally, a person who sweats, that is, worries.

clue.text: Make out with date

definitions.meaning: to make out is to discern with the eyes
to date someone is to go out with them

explanation.surface: Romantic slang: kissing someone you are dating.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both perceiving something and courting someone regularly.

clue.text: Do motorist: drink shows up

parts.note: to do someone is to cheat them, to screw them
a driver is a motorist

explanation.surface: An instruction to cheat a motorist, as a drinker turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' is slang for swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a cocktail of vodka and orange juice.

clue.text: Open Hello! — event getting spread

indicators.note: spread means scattered about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A magazine launch event covered by a spread in Hello!, the celebrity magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: Hello! is a British celebrity magazine; its letters with EVENT are shuffled by 'spread'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being honest and above board is being open, an idiom from a builder's level surface.

clue.text: Remove poster found in Morecambe by end of June

indicators.note: found in means the poster word sits inside the comedian's name

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was the comedian of the duo Morecambe and Wise
an ad is an advert, such as a poster
at can mean by, as in at the window

indicators.note: end of asks for the final letter of the word June

explanation.surface: A poster turned up in the seaside town of Morecambe by late June.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a Lancashire seaside town, but here it is Eric Morecambe, the British TV comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to wipe out entirely, a stronger synonym for removing.

clue.text: Son stops drivers parking right now

indicators.note: stops means plugs, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British drivers' organisation
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A son stopping cars from parking immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the UK's Automobile Association, a motoring breakdown club.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for as soon as possible demands action immediately.

clue.text: Cut up rubbish suit

indicators.note: in a down light, up means the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: to snip is to cut
tripe means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Tearing up a suit someone considers rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SNIP into PINS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinstripe is a business suit made from cloth with fine stripes.

clue.text: Muse close to Lucian smeared with oil paint

indicators.note: smeared means messed about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word Muse placed next to the close, the final letter, of Lucian

explanation.surface: The muse of painter Lucian Freud daubed in oil paint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close to Lucian' means its last letter, N, set beside MUSE. 'oil paint' looks like one phrase, but 'oil' is anagram fodder; 'paint' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Emulsion is the water-based paint used on walls.

clue.text: Centre to massage with rub down

indicators.note: centre to asks for the middle letter of the word massage

parts.note: and means with, together with

explanation.surface: A massage centre offering rubdowns.
explanation.definitionFit: To sand wood is to smooth it with abrasive paper, rubbing it down.

clue.text: Security person turned over identification

indicators.note: turned over means read upside down, from the bottom up

parts.note: a gateman guards an entrance

explanation.surface: A guard turning over someone's ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A badge with someone's name pinned on it is how they are identified at a conference.

clue.text: Plant with a label and band name

parts.note: a term is a label or name for something
ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra, a rock band

explanation.surface: A record label deciding on a name for a band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'label' reads as a record company but is a term; ELO is the Electric Light Orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The melon is the fruit of a trailing vine, so the word names the plant.

clue.text: Student and lecturer to make most of time

parts.note: to earn is to make money

indicators.note: most of means the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Advice that pupil and teacher should make the most of their time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of time' drops the last letter from ERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is a pupil, someone being taught.

clue.text: One pegs out pants

parts.note: un is French for one
to peg out is slang for to die

explanation.surface: Someone hanging underwear on a washing line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pegs out' suggests clothes pegs on a washing line, but is slang for dying. Pants are underpants in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Undies is informal for underwear, which British English also calls pants.

clue.text: Order online: ad is about male concerned with length?

indicators.note: about means the shuffled letters go round the next piece
order as a verb means arrange, so the letters are put in a new sequence

explanation.surface: An online advert ordering something, about a man worried about his size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order online' looks like shopping, but 'Order' is the anagram signal, and 'about' puts the shuffled letters round M.
explanation.definitionFit: Length is one dimension of measurement, so something relating to it is of dimensions; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Midge swallowed by medic, an artist

indicators.note: swallowed by means the singer goes inside the doctor letters

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, a medic
Midge Ure is the Scottish singer of Ultravox

explanation.surface: A tiny insect swallowed by a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Midge' looks like an insect but is Midge Ure, singer with Ultravox and co-organiser of Live Aid.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Dürer was a German Renaissance painter and engraver.

clue.text: Hotel in good position

indicators.note: in means the letter is put inside the word for good

parts.note: nice means good or pleasant
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel in a prime location.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is one's suitable place or role, a position that fits.

clue.text: Court following a law

indicators.note: following means the court letters come after a

explanation.surface: A court proceeding according to a statute.
explanation.definitionFit: An Act of Parliament is a law passed by the legislature.

clue.text: Sending back case, not opening wine …

indicators.note: sending back means the remaining letters are read in reverse
not opening means the first letter of the word is left off

parts.note: a canister is a container or case

explanation.surface: Someone returning an unopened case of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: CANISTER loses its first letter to give ANISTER, which 'Sending back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: … check one against another?

definitions.note: the clue continues the previous one, so another means another wine

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
the Roman numeral I is one
anti means opposed to, against

explanation.surface: Continuing from the wine clue: checking one item against another.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 26, so 'another' means another wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Chianti is a red from Tuscany, a second wine following the Greek one in the clue before.

clue.text: Tender working with surgeries?

indicators.note: working means being worked into new shapes, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A carer employed alongside doctors' practices.
explanation.walkthrough: A tender is one who tends, a carer; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualified hospital nurse cares for patients and works in operating theatres and clinics.
